The size scan and later load pass can read beyond the archive, potentially faulting or consuming unrelated memory; malformed members may also advance the cursor unpredictably. This is separate from EK9426's 32-bit `pkg_size` wrap and EK723's broader package-record length validation. **Affected configuration:** AArch64 Raspberry Pi bootstrap with a PKG initrd; no checked-in firmware package with the malformed shape was found. **Confidence:** high for trusting the embedded lengths without comparison to the initrd boundary; no package or boot was used. Validate the package header and every name/data extent with overflow-safe checks against `pkg_size` before reading or loading. Source-only; see the [BSP package extent trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L6181).

<a id="ek9431"></a>
### EK9431 — m68k CyberGraphX thunks return native pointers that are not mapped into the guest.

The generated m68k CyberGraphX thunk converts the guest bitmap to its native shadow, calls `LockBitMapTagList()`, and returns the native function result unchanged (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:525-533`). For a HIDD bitmap using a CyberGraphX pixel format, the native implementation returns the native `BitMap *` as its lock handle (`workbench/libs/cgfx/lockbitmaptaglist.c:127-198`). The paired generated `UnLockBitMap()` thunk treats guest A0 as a guest/ shadow address through `THUNK_PTR` (`m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:535-541`); `m68k_to_host_or_shadow()` looks up only guest shadow addresses, then guest-arena addresses, and has no reverse mapping from a native pointer (`m68kemu_intern.h:115-126`). Consequently, a guest caller cannot reliably pass the native lock result back through the paired unlock thunk; the returned pointer may be truncated to guest D0 width and fails the expected mapping. **Trigger and consequence:** emulated m68k code locks a HIDD bitmap with a CyberGraphX pixel format, receives the native bitmap pointer, then passes that result to `UnLockBitMap()`. The native unlock path may receive NULL or a different guest-arena object instead of the locked bitmap, leaving the lock unreleased or failing to unlock it. **Affected configuration:** hosted m68kemu with a CyberGraphX library client using such a bitmap; the checked-in caller census did not establish a maintained guest invocation. **Confidence:** high for the unmatched native-return/guest-argument conversions; no guest lock was run. Return a guest shadow handle and resolve it on unlock, or translate the native result back to its existing guest bitmap shadow. Source-only; see the [lock-handle conversion trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L7648).

<a id="ek9445"></a>
### EK9445 — m68k CyberGraphX bitmap lock writes a native-width pointer into a 32-bit guest output slot.

The public `LBMI_BASEADDRESS` tag returns the bitmap base address through a caller-supplied pointer; the m68k CyberGraphX ABI provides a four-byte guest pointer/output slot (`workbench/devs/diskimage/include/amigaos/cybergraphx/cybergraphics.h:145-157`). The generated lock thunk translates its TagItem list to native layout, preserving the guest output pointer as a host pointer into the emulated arena (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_shadow.c:139-163`), then calls native `LockBitMapTagList()` (`m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:525-533`). The native implementation stores `baseaddress` through an `IPTR *` (`workbench/libs/cgfx/lockbitmaptaglist.c:150-153`). On a 64-bit host, this writes eight bytes into the four-byte guest output slot, overwriting the adjacent four bytes. **Trigger and consequence:** an emulated guest requests `LBMI_BASEADDRESS` while locking a CyberGraphX HIDD bitmap on a 64-bit hosted m68kemu target. The native-width store exceeds the guest slot and can corrupt the following guest field. **Affected configuration:** 64-bit hosts running the optional m68kemu CyberGraphX thunk, conditional on that tag and a valid guest output address. **Confidence:** high for the four-byte guest ABI slot, host-width `IPTR` store and translated destination; no bitmap lock or guest memory write was run. Use a 32-bit guest temporary and explicitly copy the representable value back after the native call. Source-only; see the [base-address width trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L7648).

<a id="ek9432"></a>
### EK9432 — m68kemu thunks pass host pointers and native structures across the guest API boundary.

The optional generated-thunk bridge returns several native object pointers as raw `IPTR` values. ASL adds the same paired-handle failure: `AllocFileRequest()` and `AllocAslRequest()` return native requester pointers directly (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:39-65`), while `FreeFileRequest()`, `RequestFile()`, and `FreeAslRequest()` resolve their requester arguments through `THUNK_PTR()` (`:42-75`). The selected native allocators use `AllocAslRequest()` to allocate requester storage (`workbench/libs/asl/allocfilerequest.c:48`; `allocaslrequest.c:48-147`). Thus an emulated caller cannot reliably use or free the returned requester handle; this extends EK9432’s pointer-return bridge scope and is conditional on guest use of these ASL vectors. For example, Icon's `GetDiskObject()`, `GetDefDiskObject()`, `GetDiskObjectNew()`, `DupDiskObjectA()` and `NewDiskObject()` return native `DiskObject *` values directly (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:4462-4467,4509-4514,4523-4528,4537-4546,4585-4590`; public signatures in `workbench/libs/icon/icon.conf:22,29,31,36,40`). IFFParse similarly returns native pointers directly: `AllocIFF()` (`m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:4634-4638`), `FindProp()`, `FindCollection()`, `FindPropContext()`, `CurrentChunk()`, `ParentChunk()`, `AllocLocalItem()`, `LocalItemData()`, `FindLocalItem()`, and `OpenClipboard()` (`:4815-4867,4888-4897,4943-4948`). These are documented pointer results (`workbench/libs/iffparse/iffparse.conf:17-18,38-47`); none is converted with `host_to_m68k()` or registered as a shadow. The generated layout tables include an `IFFHandle` shadow layout (m68k 12 bytes, native 16 bytes), and `IFFHandle` is classified for input shadow lookup, but `AllocIFF()` is absent from the generator’s `SHADOW_RETURNS` map (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:1881-1886`; `m68kemu_thunkgen.py:175-194,223-231`). Its generated wrapper therefore remains a direct native-pointer return rather than a guest shadow. In particular, an emulated `AllocIFF()` result passed to `OpenIFF()` or `FreeIFF()` is narrowed into guest D0 and then resolved by `THUNK_PTR()` as a guest-arena address or shadow, rather than the native allocation; local-item and clipboard handles have the same return-to-argument gap. Utility `SetMem()` has the same round-trip defect: its generated thunk resolves guest A0 with `THUNK_PTR(0)` and returns native `SetMem()`'s result unchanged (`m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:7146-7152`), although the public API specifies that the result is the destination address (`rom/utility/utility.conf:93`; native body returns `destination`, `rom/utility/setmem.c:89`). For a guest address in the emulator arena, the thunk therefore returns `ctx->mem + guest_address` as D0 rather than the original guest address; the dispatcher narrows the pointer to 32 bits. The shadow-aware resolver can also return a native shadow pointer, which likewise has no reverse mapping here. A guest that consumes the documented return value cannot reliably use it as its original guest pointer.

DOS `DosGetString()` also returns a native `STRPTR` unchanged (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:1796-1800`; public declaration `rom/dos/dos.conf:219`). The native routine returns a pointer into the DOS error-string table or a static fallback (`rom/dos/dosgetstring.c:40-83`), and dispatch narrows it into guest D0. A guest caller cannot reliably dereference the returned text pointer. Unlike `FilePart()`/`PathPart()`, this points to native-owned string storage rather than the guest arena.

The DOS `FilePart()` and `PathPart()` thunks also return pointers into their input strings without converting them back to guest offsets (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:1690-1702`). Both inputs are translated to host pointers into `ctx->mem`; the native functions return interior pointers into those strings (`rom/dos/filepart.c:63-83`; `rom/dos/pathpart.c:53-82`), then the dispatcher narrows the host pointer into guest D0 (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_moira.cpp:256-267`). A guest using either documented result as a string pointer therefore gets a host address fragment instead of the corresponding guest address. This applies even though the input storage is guest-owned, and is distinct from native-object handle returns. No maintained emulated caller was established.

The generated DOS `Info()` thunk passes `parameterBlock` through `THUNK_DPTR()` directly to native `Info()` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:948-954`; public declaration `rom/dos/dos.conf:72`). Native DOS forwards that same address in `ACTION_INFO` (`rom/dos/info.c:44-63`), and the selected RAM handler writes all `struct InfoData` fields through it (`rom/filesys/ram/handler.c:278-288`; `commands.c:1679-1700`; the RAM handler has an explicit `kernel-fs-ram` target in `rom/filesys/ram/mmakefile.src`). The RAM handler is an example path, not a claim of default package inclusion. The m68k guest `InfoData` is 36 bytes, while the 64-bit AROS layout is 48 bytes, with widened `BPTR`/`IPTR` fields (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:2240-2253`; `compiler/include/dos/dos.h:176-205`). Thus a successful handler write can extend 12 bytes past the guest structure and places the volume/in-use fields at host offsets instead of guest offsets; on little-endian hosts, the numeric fields also retain host byte order. This is conditional on an emulated guest calling `Info()` with a 36-byte guest buffer and the selected handler completing `ACTION_INFO`; no maintained emulated caller was found. It is another direct-structure instance of EK9432, not a separate root cause.

DOS `GetArgStr()` is another direct pointer-return instance: the generated wrapper returns native `GetArgStr()` unchanged (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:1350-1353`), while the native routine returns `Process.pr_Arguments` (`rom/dos/getargstr.c:42-57`; public signature `rom/dos/dos.conf:143`). The dispatcher writes the result into the guest 32-bit D0 (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_moira.cpp:235-267`), so on supported 64-bit hosts a guest caller receives a truncated host address instead of a guest string address and cannot reliably read the documented argument string. This adds a borrowed string result to the same guest/native return-boundary defect; no maintained emulated caller was established.

Intuition `ViewAddress()` also returns an unmapped native pointer: the generated thunk returns `ViewAddress()` directly (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:5307-5310`), and the native routine returns `&IntuitionBase->ViewLord` (`rom/intuition/viewaddress.c:15-16,48`). Dispatch narrows the host pointer into guest D0 (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_moira.cpp:256-275`); the guest receives neither a guest address nor a registered View shadow. A client that reads the documented `struct View *` or passes it to Graphics `LoadView()` cannot reliably use it. **Trigger and consequence:** an emulated client calls `ViewAddress()` and consumes the returned pointer; it gets a truncated host address. **Affected configuration:** optional m68kemu on supported hosted targets. No maintained emulated caller was established. Return a synchronized View shadow or a guest-side view address. Source-only; no view was read or loaded.

Graphics `TextExtent()`, `FontExtent()`, and `TextFit()` pass `struct TextExtent *` buffers directly to native code (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:3755-3778,3840-3847`). The structure consists of six 16-bit fields (`compiler/include/graphics/text.h:162-169`), and native implementations write those fields without guest byte-order conversion (`rom/graphics/textextent.c:62-152`; `fontextent.c:102-107`; `textfit.c:80-122`). `TextFit()` also reads an optional guest `constrainingExtent` in native byte order (`textfit.c:83-90,113-118`). On little-endian hosts the results are byte-swapped in guest memory, and a supplied constraint is interpreted with swapped dimensions/edges; text metrics and fit decisions are therefore wrong. **Trigger and consequence:** an emulated m68k client requests text extents or passes a constraint on a little-endian host; it receives corrupted metrics or TextFit makes an incorrect fit decision. **Affected configuration:** optional m68kemu on little-endian supported hosts. No maintained emulated caller was found. Marshal the fields between guest and native byte order. Source-only; no text operation was run.

Graphics `CMove()` mishandles its register-address argument. The generated thunk resolves D0 with `THUNK_DPTR()` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:3296-3303`), which returns NULL for an unmapped address outside the 32-MB guest arena (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_intern.h:20,114-124`). But `CMove()` expects D0 to encode a custom-chip register address: `CMOVE()` passes `&custom.xxx` (`compiler/include/graphics/gfxmacros.h:50-53`), and the native function masks the address to the Copper register offset (`rom/graphics/cmove.c:55-60`). For a conventional guest custom register address such as `0xDFF180`, the resolver supplies NULL and native code emits destination offset zero instead of `0x180`. **Trigger and consequence:** guest Copper-list code calls `CMove()`/`CMOVE()` with a custom-register address; the generated instruction targets the wrong register. **Affected configuration:** the optional m68kemu Graphics bridge. No maintained emulated caller was found. Preserve this argument as its guest register value and translate the hardware address to the expected Copper offset rather than resolving it as an arena pointer. Source-only; no copper list was run.

Graphics `PolyDraw()` also receives guest coordinate storage without ABI conversion: the thunk passes its `WORD *polyTable` through `THUNK_PTR()` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:3268-3277`; prototype `rom/graphics/graphics.conf:96`). Native Graphics reads `count` pairs of `WORD` coordinates directly (`rom/graphics/polydraw.c:55-63`). On little-endian hosts these words remain in guest big-endian byte order, so coordinate `0x0100` is read as `0x0001` and lines are drawn at the wrong points. **Trigger and consequence:** an emulated m68k client calls `PolyDraw()` with a non-byte-symmetric coordinate on a little-endian host; the polyline geometry is corrupted. **Affected configuration:** optional m68kemu on little-endian supported hosts. No maintained emulated caller was found. Marshal the coordinate pairs to native-endian words before dispatch. Source-only; no drawing call was run.

Graphics `LoadRGB4()` is a distinct raw-data instance: its thunk passes the guest `UWORD *colors` straight through `THUNK_PTR()` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:3081-3088`; resolver `rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_intern.h:114-124`). Native `LoadRGB4()` indexes those words and extracts the documented `0x0RGB` components without byte swapping (`rom/graphics/loadrgb4.c:62-98`; public declaration `rom/graphics/graphics.conf:72`). On little-endian hosts, a guest big-endian word such as `0x0F00` is read as `0x000F`, changing red 15 into blue 15. **Trigger and consequence:** an emulated m68k client passes a non-byte-symmetric palette word to `LoadRGB4()` on a little-endian host; the resulting palette colors are channel-swapped. **Affected configuration:** optional m68kemu on little-endian supported hosts. No maintained in-tree guest caller was found. Marshal the word array into native-endian storage for the duration of the call. Source-only; no screen or palette update was run.

The generated Graphics thunks have the same missing reverse mapping for the eight non-destructive Region APIs: `AndRectRegionND()`, `AndRegionRegionND()`, `OrRectRegionND()`, `OrRegionRegionND()`, `XorRectRegionND()`, `XorRegionRegionND()`, `ClearRectRegionND()`, and `ClearRegionRegionND()` return their native `struct Region *` directly as `IPTR` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:4314-4319,4323-4327,4330-4335,4339-4343,4346-4351,4355-4359,4362-4367,4371-4375`; public return declarations `rom/graphics/graphics.conf:232-239`). Unlike the `NewRegion()` thunk (`:3485-3491`), these wrappers neither register a guest shadow nor return a guest-arena address. The thunk dispatcher narrows the host pointer into guest D0, and a subsequent `DisposeRegion()` or other Region-vector call resolves that value only as a registered shadow or guest-arena address (`m68kemu_moira.cpp:256-275`; `m68kemu_intern.h:114-125`; `m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:3511-3515`). Thus a guest Region result cannot reliably be inspected, passed to another Region API, or disposed; the native allocation is also not reachable through its documented handle. This is distinct from EK9440's stale fields in the valid `NewRegion()` shadow and EK9438's release of that shadow. No maintained in-tree guest caller of the non-destructive Region vectors was found; this remains conditional on emulated clients using them. No guest Region call or build was run; source-only.

The generated-thunk dispatcher puts the returned value into guest D0 by narrowing `IPTR` to `u32` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_moira.cpp:256-275`). A subsequent thunk argument is resolved by `m68k_to_host_or_shadow()`, which recognizes only registered guest shadows or an address within the guest memory arena (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_intern.h:114-125`). These Icon and IFFParse return paths do not create corresponding shadows. Consequently the guest cannot reliably pass a returned object back to `PutDiskObject()`/`FreeDiskObject()` or `OpenIFF()`/`FreeIFF()`; on 64-bit hosts the pointer is first truncated, and a resulting value that happens to fall within guest memory is treated as an unrelated guest address. The guest also cannot safely inspect returned native structures. The checked-in layout descriptions show an `IFFHandle` of 12 guest bytes versus 16 native bytes, a `ContextNode` of 24 versus 32 bytes, and a `StoredProperty` of 8 versus 16 bytes (`m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:639-646,1881-1886,3657-3661`); merely passing guest-allocated storage through the existing pointer resolver does not convert those layouts.

The Commodities `CopyBrokerList()` and `FreeBrokerList()` wrappers pass guest `struct List *` arguments directly to native code (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:319-331`). `CopyBrokerList()` first calls `FreeBrokerList(CopyofList)` and then appends native `BrokerCopy` nodes (`workbench/libs/commodities/copybrokerlist.c:63-90`); `FreeBrokerList()` repeatedly calls native `RemHead()` and frees each returned node (`freebrokerlist.c:56-60`). The guest `List` and `Node` contain 32-bit big-endian pointer fields (`compiler/include/exec/lists.h:31-48`; `exec/nodes.h:31-47`), while the selected little-endian 64-bit hosts use native-width pointers. No List/Node shadow is created by these wrappers. Consequently native `RemHead()` reads guest list links using incompatible pointer width, offsets, and byte order; even an initialized empty guest list can be interpreted as a nonempty list or invalid pointer and cause an invalid host read/free before copying begins. Any nodes later appended are likewise native-layout nodes, not guest-layout nodes. This is the Commodities list-argument case of the same marshalling boundary, separate from EK9893's `NewBroker` structure mismatch.

The same raw-pointer boundary also affects Locale's `DateStamp` arguments. The generated `FormatDate()` and `ParseDate()` wrappers resolve A2/A1 with `THUNK_PTR()` and pass the guest record directly (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:6587-6595,6734-6742`). `m68k_to_host_or_shadow()` falls back to the guest arena unless an exact shadow is already registered (`m68kemu_intern.h:115-125`); these wrappers do not create a `DateStamp` shadow. Although the declared record is 12 bytes with three 32-bit fields on both sides, the guest fields are big-endian (`compiler/include/dos/datetime.h:14-28`; `m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:832-838`) while the supported x86-64, AArch64, and RISC-V hosts are little-endian. Native `FormatDate()` reads `ds_Days`, `ds_Minute`, and `ds_Tick` as host `LONG`s (`workbench/libs/locale/formatdate.c:128-143`); `ParseDate()` writes those same fields through the raw pointer (`parsedate.c:410-434`). Thus, for an ordinary guest-owned record, formatting interprets byte-reversed values and parsing returns byte-reversed fields to the guest. This Locale structure case is separate from EK9894's Hook callback execution issue, but shares EK9432's unconverted guest/native argument root cause. DOS `SetFileDate()` has the same input case: its generated wrapper resolves D2 through `THUNK_DPTR()` and passes the guest `DateStamp *` unchanged (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:1181-1187`). Native `SetFileDate()` forwards that address as `ACTION_SET_DATE` packet data (`rom/dos/setfiledate.c:57-67`); selected RAMFS copies the 12 raw bytes into its native date record (`rom/filesys/ram/commands.c:2058-2083`), preserving the guest's big-endian byte order as incorrect host field values. On little-endian hosts, a normal guest date is therefore stored with byte-reversed fields. DOS `DateStamp()` has the corresponding output case: its generated thunk resolves D1 with `THUNK_DPTR()` and passes the guest record directly (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:994-1001`), while native `DateStamp()` writes the three 32-bit fields in host byte order (`rom/dos/datestamp.c:70-91`). The 12-byte layouts match, but on little-endian hosts a guest observes each returned field byte-reversed. The wrapper also returns native `DateStamp()`'s pointer in D0 without mapping it back to the guest address; consuming that documented pointer result therefore gives the guest an unusable host-address fragment. These consequences are conditional on a guest calling the optional vector and consuming the output or result, and are EK9432 instances, not separate root causes. `SetFileDate()` is another manifestation of the same unconverted guest/native argument boundary.

The generated `GetSegListInfo()` wrapper converts its guest TagItem list with `m68k_to_native_taglist()` and calls native DOS (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:1828-1835`). For `GSLI_ElfHandle` and `GSLI_68KHUNK`, the native implementation treats `ti_Data` as `IPTR *` and writes the handle there (`rom/dos/getseglistinfo.c:78-96`). On the supported 64-bit hosts `IPTR` is 8 bytes, while the m68k guest slot is 4 bytes; the tag converter maps an ordinary guest output-slot address to `ctx->mem + address` (`m68kemu_shadow.c:146-159`). A matching segment and either recognized tag therefore make native code write an 8-byte value into the guest's 4-byte slot, overwriting its following four bytes. This is conditional on the guest having a `seglist` BPTR that matches a DOS-tracked native segment; no checked-in m68kemu caller for this vector was found.

`CxBroker()` also writes a scalar output through a guest pointer without guest-endian conversion. Its generated thunk resolves D0 with `THUNK_DPTR()` and passes the resulting arena address as `LONG *` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:119-125`); the resolver returns `ctx->mem + addr` for ordinary guest memory (`m68kemu_intern.h:115-125`). Native `CxBroker()` writes nonzero results with `*error = myerr` (`workbench/libs/commodities/cxbroker.c:145-151`); the public error values include `CBERR_SYSERR=1` and `CBERR_DUP=2` (`compiler/include/libraries/commodities.h:55-58`). Guest m68k 32-bit reads are explicitly big-endian (`m68kemu_intern.h:141-147`), while the selected x86-64, AArch64, and RISC-V hosts are little-endian. Thus a native write of `CBERR_SYSERR` leaves bytes `01 00 00 00` in guest memory, which guest code reads as `0x01000000`. This is conditional on a non-NULL guest error pointer and `CxBroker()` reaching a nonzero error return; its separate `NewBroker` input-layout mismatch remains EK9893. This output case shares EK9432's direct guest-memory marshalling cause rather than establishing a separate root cause.

The generated DOS `ErrorReport()` thunk also forwards D3 `arg1` as an unchanged integer (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:1290-1297`). For `REPORT_VOLUME`, native `ErrorReport()` casts it to `DeviceList *` and reads `dl_Name`/`dl_Task` (`rom/dos/errorreport.c:192-200`), but the guest structure is 44 bytes with `dl_Name` at offset 40 while the 64-bit native structure is 80 bytes with `dl_Name` at offset 72 (`compiler/include/dos/dosextens.h:438-455`; `m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:940-953`); this call path creates no DeviceList shadow. For `REPORT_INSERT`, native code treats the same D3 value as a host C string and passes it into `getpacketinfo()` (`errorreport.c:210-223`), so a guest arena address is used as an unmapped host address. The affected values are interpreted only when `ErrorReport()` proceeds past its disabled-requester guard and handles the corresponding error/type combination.

The generated DOS list and path helpers have related unconverted pointer results. `LockDosList()` and `AttemptLockDosList()` return native `DosList *` values directly, while `FindDosEntry()` and `NextDosEntry()` resolve their input cursor with `THUNK_DPTR()` and return native entries directly (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:1486-1504,1521-1535`; public signatures and cursor contract in `rom/dos/dos.conf:164-169`, `rom/dos/finddosentry.c:20-34`, and `nextdosentry.c:20-31`). Although a `DosList` layout descriptor is registered (`m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:1186-1197,4494`), these wrappers do not create or translate a guest shadow. Thus a normal guest lock-and-iterate sequence cannot round-trip the returned native cursor through the guest address resolver, and a guest that inspects a returned entry also sees a host-layout object. `FindVar()` similarly returns a native `LocalVar *` without creating its registered shadow (`m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:1757-1763`; descriptor at `m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:2499-2510,4573`), so guest code cannot reliably read its pointer-bearing fields. `FilePart()` and `PathPart()` return pointers into their guest input string, but their wrappers return the host pointer from `m68k_to_host()` directly (`m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:1691-1699`; documented interior-pointer results in `rom/dos/dos.conf:200-201`, `rom/dos/filepart.c:35-50`, and `pathpart.c:30-45`). The dispatcher narrows each raw `IPTR` to guest D0 and does not call the available `host_to_m68k()` helper (`m68kemu_moira.cpp:256-275`; helper at `m68kemu_intern.h:127-130`), so these APIs return host addresses rather than guest addresses. These are additional DOS instances of EK9432's existing guest/native pointer-boundary cause, not separate findings. No maintained in-tree m68k guest caller of these vectors was established.

The generated Exec list primitives have the same direct-layout problem: `Insert()`, `AddHead()`, `AddTail()`, `Remove()`, `RemHead()`, `RemTail()`, and `Enqueue()` resolve guest `List *`/`Node *` arguments with `THUNK_PTR()` and call native Exec directly; `RemHead()` and `RemTail()` also return native node pointers without reverse translation (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:1917-1967`; vector signatures in `rom/exec/exec.conf:112-118`). The generated shadow map describes guest `List`/`Node` layouts as 14 bytes and native layouts as 32 bytes, but these wrappers do not create those shadows (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:2470-2480,2858-2867,4570,4598`). For example, selected native `AddHead()` writes native-width `ln_Succ`/`ln_Pred` pointers into the guest node and list fields at host offsets (`rom/exec/addhead.c:52-66`), which do not match the 32-bit guest offsets; `AddTail()` does likewise (`rom/exec/addtail.c:49-63`). Guest list links can consequently be overwritten with incompatible host pointer widths/offsets, and returned nodes do not round-trip as guest addresses. This extends EK9432's existing guest/native structure-marshalling cause; no maintained in-tree m68k guest caller was established.

The generated Exec private-memory list wrappers also pass guest structures straight to native code. `Allocate()`/`Deallocate()` pass the guest `MemHeader *` and block pointer through `THUNK_PTR()`; `AllocEntry()` passes a guest `MemList *` the same way, returns the native `MemList *` unchanged, and `FreeEntry()` resolves that result as if it were a guest address (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:1872-1909`; API signatures in `rom/exec/exec.conf:108-111`). The registered descriptors show `MemHeader` as 32 guest bytes versus 72 native bytes and `MemList` as 24 guest bytes versus 56 native bytes (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:2594-2620,2609-2620`); these wrappers do not create shadows. Native allocation code therefore reads guest fields at incompatible offsets, and an `AllocEntry()` result cannot be passed back through `FreeEntry()` as its native allocation handle. This is another instance of EK9432's existing boundary cause; no maintained in-tree guest caller of these vectors was found.

The generated Exec task-creation and Expansion thunks expose the same boundary. `NewCreateTaskA()` converts its guest tag list, but returns the native `Task *` unchanged; the public vector returns `struct Task *` (`rom/exec/exec.conf:236`; thunk at `m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:2467-2473`). A guest that uses that result as a task pointer has neither a guest shadow nor a reverse-mapped address. `NewStackSwap()` likewise passes its `StackSwapStruct *`, function pointer, and `StackSwapArgs *` through the raw pointer resolver (`:2378-2384`), leaving both guest structure layout and callback-address interpretation unconverted. The Expansion wrappers pass `ConfigDev *` inputs/results directly (`:2520-2675`); this includes `AllocConfigDev()`'s native allocation result, `FindConfigDev()` cursor/result, and the add/configure/free/read/write operations. The registered descriptor identifies `ConfigDev` as 68 guest bytes versus 112 native bytes with translated pointer fields (`m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:611-633,4456`). `SetCurrentBinding()` and `GetCurrentBinding()` also pass a guest buffer directly to native code (`m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:2658-2675`); the registered `CurrentBinding` layout is 16 guest bytes versus 32 native bytes (`m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:697-701,4463`). These calls therefore read or write incompatible offsets, pointer widths, and byte order, and returned native pointers cannot reliably round-trip through guest addresses. These are additional instances of EK9432's existing boundary cause. No maintained in-tree m68k guest caller for these vectors was established. GadTools' `GetVisualInfoA()` / `FreeVisualInfo()` pair has the same unpaired pointer boundary: the generated getter returns native `APTR` directly, and the free thunk applies `THUNK_PTR()` to the guest value (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:2846-2862`; public signatures in `workbench/libs/gadtools/gadtools.conf:51-52`). The API defines the returned visual-info object as input to `FreeVisualInfo()` (`workbench/libs/gadtools/getvisualinfoa.c:28-30,47`; `freevisualinfo.c:24-39`), but no guest shadow or reverse mapping is created. A guest create/free cycle therefore cannot reliably pass the handle back to the native free routine; pointer truncation on 64-bit hosts may also make the returned value unusable. This is another existing EK9432 bridge instance, not a separate root cause.

The Graphics `AllocRaster()`/`FreeRaster()` pair also lacks a guest handle mapping: the allocator thunk returns the native `PLANEPTR` directly, and the free thunk resolves the guest value with `THUNK_PTR()` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:3450-3466`; public pair contract in `rom/graphics/graphics.conf:122-123` and `freeraster.c:27-31`). The returned host allocation therefore cannot reliably be supplied back as a guest pointer to free the plane. IFFParse `OpenClipboard()`/`CloseClipboard()` likewise return and consume an unmapped native `ClipboardHandle *` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:4943-4957`; `workbench/libs/iffparse/iffparse.conf:53-54`). Intuition `CurrentTime()` passes guest `seconds` and `micros` storage straight to native code (`m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:5021-5028`); native code stores two host `ULONG`s (`rom/intuition/currenttime.c:55-58`), so on little-endian hosts the guest big-endian fields are byte-reversed. These are further instances of the established pointer/structure boundary; no maintained in-tree emulated caller was found.

The Graphics `GfxNew()`/`GfxFree()` and `OpenMonitor()`/`CloseMonitor()` pairs expose the same handle mismatch. Their generated getters return native `ExtendedNode *` and `MonitorSpec *` values directly, while the matching free/close thunks resolve the guest value through `THUNK_PTR()` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:3715-3729,3798-3814`; signatures in `rom/graphics/graphics.conf:157-162`). `GfxNew()` allocates native memory and `GfxFree()` dereferences and frees that pointer (`rom/graphics/gfxnew.c:72-109`; `gfxfree.c:66-94`); `OpenMonitor()` returns either a native monitor-list entry or the native default monitor and `CloseMonitor()` dereferences its semaphore/open-count fields (`openmonitor.c:76-99`; `closemonitor.c:55-72`). These documented pairs cannot reliably round-trip through guest D0/A0 on the supported 64-bit host bridge. No maintained in-tree emulated guest caller for these vectors was established.

The Graphics `LoadRGB32()` and `GetRGB32()` vectors also use unconverted guest `ULONG` arrays (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:4015-4040`; signatures in `rom/graphics/graphics.conf:147,150`). `LoadRGB32()` reads the guest table through native `ULONG *` accesses, while `GetRGB32()` writes native `ULONG` values into the guest output array (`rom/graphics/loadrgb32.c:56-87`; `getrgb32.c:57-65`). On the supported little-endian hosts, ordinary m68k big-endian 32-bit color entries are therefore byte-reversed on input or output. This is another endian instance of the same unconverted guest/native boundary; no maintained emulated caller was established. The `GetRGB32()` thunk also resolves its `ColorMap *` with `m68k_to_host()` rather than the shadow-aware resolver (`m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:4035-4040`; resolver definitions in `m68kemu_intern.h:107-125`). A guest `GetColorMap()` call returns a registered 52-byte m68k `ColorMap` shadow while the selected x86-64 native layout is 96 bytes (`m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:3568-3574`; `m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:454-475,4450`). Passing that guest address to `GetRGB32()` therefore makes the native vector interpret guest shadow bytes as a native object; on x86-64 it reads `ColorTable` at native offset 8, where the guest shadow instead stores `cm_vpe` (which is normally NULL), and `color_get()` dereferences that table for each requested color (`rom/graphics/getrgb32.c:57-65`; `color_support.c:87-104`). This makes the documented `GetColorMap()` then `GetRGB32()` sequence fail for nonzero color counts, in addition to the separate output-array endian issue. The vector argument should resolve through the ColorMap shadow before native dispatch. The same generated slice contains five region APIs—`ScrollRegion()`, `AndRectRegionND()`, `OrRectRegionND()`, `XorRectRegionND()`, and `ClearRectRegionND()`—whose `struct Rectangle *` arguments are passed through `THUNK_PTR()` directly (`m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:4304-4319,4330-4335,4346-4351,4362-4367`). For an ordinary guest-owned rectangle, the resolver returns its raw arena address and does not convert its four big-endian `WORD` fields (`compiler/include/graphics/gfx.h:45-51`). The native functions read those fields as host words; on little-endian hosts non-byte-symmetric coordinates are byte-reversed, so the intersection, union, xor, clear, or scroll uses the wrong rectangle. `ScrollRegion()` feeds the rectangle to the region-intersection and clipping operations (`rom/graphics/scrollregion.c:65-80`). This is another concrete raw-structure input instance of EK9432; no maintained guest caller was established.

`GetDisplayInfoData()` has the same unconverted output-buffer boundary for all four public tags, not only `DTAG_MNTR`. Its thunk passes the guest buffer directly to native graphics code, which builds a host `DisplayInfo`, `DimensionInfo`, `MonitorInfo`, or `NameInfo` and copies the first `min(size, sizeof(native structure))` bytes without conversion (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:3829-3837`; `rom/graphics/getdisplayinfodata.c:21-28,175-187,489-504`). The registered layouts record guest/native sizes of 56/72 bytes for `DisplayInfo`, 88/96 for `DimensionInfo`, 96/112 for `MonitorInfo`, and 56/64 for `NameInfo` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:990-1002,1070-1088,2667-2684,2767-2774`). `DTAG_DISP` also diverges at `PropertyFlags` (guest offset 18, native offset 20), so fields after it are shifted as well as host-endian. `DTAG_DIMS` copies its multi-byte query header, depth/dimension words, and Rectangle coordinates in native byte order; its guest-sized copy also places the native 64-bit `reserved[0]` value into the two 32-bit guest reserved slots. `DTAG_NAME` preserves the byte-array name but returns its ULONG query-header fields in host byte order. For each tag, `QueryHeader.Length` is computed from the larger host `sizeof(structure)`, so it advertises a longer record than the guest ABI layout. `DTAG_MNTR` additionally places the 64-bit native `Mspc` pointer where the guest structure expects a 32-bit pointer, shifting later fields; the concrete 96-byte guest-buffer example is recorded in the coverage ledger. On little-endian 64-bit hosts, guest code therefore receives malformed mode records and can misread mode properties or the monitor pointer. This expands EK9432's existing `GetDisplayInfoData()` marshalling instance; it is not a separate root cause. No maintained in-tree m68k guest caller of these vectors was established.

Graphics `FindDisplayInfo()` also returns a raw native `DisplayInfoHandle *` into the per-monitor mode array (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:3812-3817`; `rom/graphics/finddisplayinfo.c:55-80`; public type `compiler/include/graphics/displayinfo.h:28`). A guest that passes that returned handle to `GetDisplayInfoData()` reaches the generated `THUNK_PTR()` conversion (`m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:3829-3837`), which accepts only a guest address or registered shadow; the native implementation then dereferences the handle’s `id` and `drv` fields (`rom/graphics/getdisplayinfodata.c:146-168`). The returned native pointer is not mapped back to guest space, so this documented handle round trip is not reliable on the 64-bit m68kemu hosts. `GetDisplayInfoData()` can instead be called with a NULL handle and the mode ID, so that supported usage avoids this specific handle defect. This is another conditional EK9432 pointer-return instance; no emulated caller was found.

The Graphics `AllocDBufInfo()`/`FreeDBufInfo()` and `AllocSpriteDataA()`/`FreeSpriteData()` pairs expose native pointers without guest shadows (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:4121-4133,4199-4225`; public vector signatures in `rom/graphics/graphics.conf:207-208,216,218`). Each allocator returns its native object pointer directly, while the corresponding free thunk resolves the guest pointer through `THUNK_PTR()`. Thus guest code cannot reliably free a returned handle, and direct access to its host-layout fields is not supported by this bridge. These are additional instances of EK9432's established pointer-boundary cause. No maintained emulated caller was found.

Intuition `GetPrefs()` and `GetDefPrefs()` copy native `struct Preferences` bytes to the caller buffer and return that buffer pointer (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:5077-5094`; signatures in `rom/intuition/intuition.conf:73-74`; native copy and return in `rom/intuition/getprefs.c:48-64` and `getdefprefs.c:47-63`). The thunk maps the guest buffer to host memory but performs no field-wise endian conversion; native 16-bit and 32-bit preference values are therefore byte-reversed in the m68k guest on little-endian hosts, and the documented returned pointer is a host address rather than the original guest address. The native copy clamps its byte count to `sizeof(struct Preferences)`, so this finding does not assert an overrun for a correctly sized or smaller buffer. `SetPrefs()` has the inverse mismatch: its thunk passes the guest `Preferences` buffer directly, and native code copies its bytes into the live structure before reading multi-byte fields (`m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:5350-5358`; `rom/intuition/setprefs.c:78-102`). On little-endian hosts, guest values are therefore stored byte-reversed in native state. This is another instance of the existing bridge defect.

The Intuition `GetScreenData()` and `QueryOverscan()` output paths also use guest buffers as native structures (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:5440-5449,5525-5533`; public signatures in `rom/intuition/intuition.conf:124,132`). `GetScreenData()` copies native `struct Screen` bytes directly into the caller buffer for the caller-supplied size (`rom/intuition/getscreendata.c:66-80`). Its documented `sizeof(struct Screen)` request copies a host-layout prefix into a guest record whose `FirstWindow` and `Title` offsets are 4/22, versus native offsets 8/32 (`compiler/include/intuition/screens.h:34-75`; `m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:3441-3460`), so pointers and fields are not usable as a guest Screen. `QueryOverscan()` copies a native `Rectangle` into guest memory (`rom/intuition/queryoverscan.c:85-106`); its four 16-bit coordinates are written in host byte order and are reversed for a big-endian guest on little-endian hosts. No overrun is claimed when the caller supplies a buffer matching the requested size. These are further manifestations of EK9432's existing bridge defect.

The generated Intuition `GadgetMouse()` and `SysReqHandler()` wrappers also pass output pointers directly into guest memory (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:5657-5664,5684-5690`; signatures in `rom/intuition/intuition.conf:149,156`). `GadgetMouse()` writes two native `WORD` coordinates through `mousepoint[0..1]` (`rom/intuition/gadgetmouse.c:73-77`); `SysReqHandler()` writes the received native `ULONG` IDCMP class when a matching event is returned (`rom/intuition/sysrequest_intern.c:283-290`). On the supported little-endian hosts these values are stored in host byte order, so a big-endian m68k guest reads byte-reversed coordinates or flag values. The outputs are conditional on the respective vector calls and, for `SysReqHandler()`, a matching IDCMP message. `SetIPrefs()` likewise forwards its guest data buffer without structure conversion (`m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:5667-5674`): its screen-mode branch reads `IScreenModePrefs` fields as native integers and therefore interprets ordinary big-endian guest fields incorrectly on little-endian hosts. `SetIPrefs()` is documented as a private vector (`rom/intuition/setiprefs.c:37-41`), and its checked-in native caller supplies a native-converted, full-size record; no maintained guest caller was found. These are additional conditional instances of the same EK9432 marshalling boundary, not independent findings.

`SetPointerBounds()` also forwards a guest `Rectangle *` directly (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:6100-6109`). When pointer bounds are inactive or still in their reset interval, native Intuition reads the four `WORD` coordinates into its mouse-bound state (`rom/intuition/setpointerbounds.c:28-52`); on little-endian hosts the values from a normal m68k Rectangle are byte-reversed. No maintained emulated caller was found.

The generated `MapRawKey()` thunk passes a guest `InputEvent *` directly to native keymap.library (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:6138-6145`). Although the native implementation ignores `ie_NextEvent`, it reads `ie_Class`, `ie_Code`, and `ie_Qualifier` at host offsets 8, 10, and 12 (`rom/keymap/maprawkey.c:85-99`), while the guest structure places those fields at offsets 4, 6, and 8 (`compiler/include/devices/inputevent.h:26-38`; `m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:2255-2262`). Thus an ordinary guest RAWKEY event is classified from its position bytes and its code/qualifier are read from later fields; it will generally be rejected or mapped incorrectly. This is another conditional guest/native structure case under EK9432; no maintained emulated caller was found.

Utility's `Amiga2Date()`, `Date2Amiga()`, and `CheckDate()` thunks pass guest `ClockData *` storage directly to native code (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:6907-6927`; public signatures in `rom/utility/utility.conf:55-57`). `Amiga2Date()` writes seven `UWORD` fields, while the other two read those fields (`rom/utility/amiga2date.c:94-98`; `date2amiga.c:65-99`; `checkdate.c:65-121`; `compiler/include/utility/date.h:16-25`). On little-endian hosts, the native code byte-reverses each guest field on output or interprets each input field byte-reversed, producing incorrect dates, seconds, or validity results. No maintained emulated guest caller was found.

The Intuition screen-buffer allocation pair has the same native-handle problem. `AllocScreenBuffer()` returns a native `ScreenBuffer *` directly; `FreeScreenBuffer()` and `ChangeScreenBuffer()` resolve the guest argument as a guest address (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:5824-5849`; signatures in `rom/intuition/intuition.conf:181-183`). Native allocation creates a host-owned `IntScreenBuffer` wrapper (`rom/intuition/allocscreenbuffer.c:89-99`), and the public free contract requires that exact result (`freescreenbuffer.c:27-33`). The guest therefore cannot reliably pass the returned handle to the corresponding free or change operation. This is another existing EK9432 instance.

The `AllocIntuiMessage()`/`FreeIntuiMessage()` and `StartScreenNotifyTagList()`/`EndScreenNotify()` Intuition pairs have the same unshadowed native-handle failure (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:6018-6064`; public signatures in `rom/intuition/intuition.conf:202-203,208-209`). Their allocating thunks return native pointers directly, while the corresponding release thunks resolve the guest value with `THUNK_PTR()`. Native `AllocIntuiMessage()` allocates an internal IntuiMessage from Intuition's pool (`rom/intuition/allocintuimessage.c:54-72`); `StartScreenNotifyTagList()` allocates and returns a notification record that `EndScreenNotify()` removes and frees (`rom/intuition/startscreennotifytaglist.c:94-112`; `endscreennotify.c:69-82`). Neither pair creates a guest shadow, so guest handles cannot reliably round-trip to their release functions. These are further instances of EK9432's established boundary cause.

Layers `NewLayerInfo()`/`DisposeLayerInfo()` also return and consume an unshadowed native `Layer_Info *` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:6343-6355`; public signatures in `rom/hyperlayers/layers.conf:38-39`). Native `NewLayerInfo()` allocates a host `Layer_Info`, initializes it, and returns it (`rom/hyperlayers/newlayerinfo.c:46-68`); `DisposeLayerInfo()` dereferences and frees the supplied pointer (`disposelayerinfo.c:46-55`). The generated result cannot reliably round-trip through the guest pointer resolver, so normal guest ownership of this public handle fails. This is another EK9432 pointer-boundary instance.

The older `InitLayers()` vector also passes an ordinary guest `Layer_Info *` straight to native code (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:6161-6166`; declaration `rom/hyperlayers/layers.conf:19`). `THUNK_PTR()` resolves normal guest memory to its arena address without structure conversion (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks.h:37`; `m68kemu_intern.h:114-125`). Native `InitLayers()` clears `sizeof(struct Layer_Info)` bytes, then initializes host-layout list and semaphore fields (`rom/hyperlayers/initlayers.c:61-70`). The registered layout metadata gives the m68k structure as 102 bytes and the selected 64-bit native structure as 768 bytes (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:2408-2427,4567`). Thus a guest supplying its normal `sizeof(struct Layer_Info)` buffer has 666 bytes beyond that object overwritten in guest memory, and the native list/semaphore writes also use incompatible offsets and pointer representation. This is a concrete writable-buffer instance of EK9432, conditional on an emulated guest calling this obsolete but exported vector with guest-owned storage; no checked-in guest caller was found.

Intuition `NextObject()` has a pointer-to-pointer layout mismatch (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:5775-5780`; declaration `rom/intuition/intuition.conf:168`). The thunk resolves A0 to the guest arena with `THUNK_PTR(0)` and forwards it unchanged. Native `NextObject()` reads and updates that argument as `struct _Object **` (`rom/intuition/nextobject.c:63-76`), but a normal m68k guest slot stores a 32-bit big-endian object pointer; selected little-endian 64-bit hosts read/write a native-width pointer instead. A guest iteration can therefore select an invalid object pointer and overwrite the adjacent guest word when advancing. Checked-in native Intuition/MUI callers use this API, but they call the native vector directly; no maintained emulated guest caller was found. This is another conditional instance of EK9432, limited to the optional m68kemu bridge.

The HyperLayers tag-list creation and query vectors contain further raw handle paths. `CreateUpfrontLayerTagList()` and `CreateBehindLayerTagList()` return native `Layer *` values directly instead of creating the shadows used by their non-tag counterparts; `ChangeLayerVisibility()`, `IsLayerVisible()`, and `IsLayerHiddenBySibling()` resolve `Layer *` arguments with `THUNK_PTR()` rather than the shadow-aware resolver (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:6489-6568`; signatures in `rom/hyperlayers/layers.conf:56-62`). Consequently a layer created by either tag-list thunk cannot reliably be passed to these query/mutation APIs or `DeleteLayer()`. This remains conditional on a usable guest `Layer_Info`/layer creation path; no maintained emulated caller was found. It shares EK9432's pointer-mapping cause and is not counted as an independent root cause.

Locale `OpenCatalogA()`/`CloseCatalog()` and `OpenLocale()`/`CloseLocale()` also fail to map their native object handles (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:6556-6570,6717-6732`; public signatures in `workbench/libs/locale/locale.conf:54-55`). The open thunks return native pointers directly, while the close thunks resolve the guest value through `THUNK_PTR()`. `GetCatalogStr()` and `GetLocaleStr()` similarly return native string pointers without translating them to guest addresses (`:6612-6628`; signatures at `locale.conf:41-42`). Thus normal guest open/use/close and string-result flows cannot reliably round-trip these handles or results. No maintained emulated caller was established; these remain optional m68kemu API bridge instances of EK9432.



The generated Exec `PutMsg()` thunk also passes an ordinary guest-owned `struct Message` directly to native Exec (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:2051-2057`; `THUNK_PTR()` resolves an unshadowed guest address to `ctx->mem + addr`, `m68kemu_thunks.h:37`, `m68kemu_intern.h:115-125`). The checked-in layout descriptor gives `Message` as 20 bytes in the m68k ABI and 48 bytes on the selected 64-bit host, with `ln_Succ`/`ln_Pred` at guest offsets 0/4 versus host offsets 0/8 (`m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:2641-2652`). `PutMsg()` sets native `mn_Node.ln_Type`, then `InternalPutMsg()` inserts the node with native-width pointers (`rom/exec/putmsg.c:60-76`; `compiler/include/exec/lists.h:123-134`). If a guest allocates a normal 20-byte message and sends it to a native-backed port such as the shadow returned by `CreateMsgPort()`, the queue operation overwrites guest fields with host-width links and writes the native node type over the guest reply-port field. This is a further input-structure instance of EK9432; no maintained in-tree emulated guest caller was found. It applies to optional m68kemu builds whose host layout has 64-bit pointers.

The handwritten `GetMsg()` bridge assumes every returned `Message *` is an `IntuiMessage *` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks.c:621-640`), although Exec declares the vector as returning the generic `struct Message *` (`rom/exec/exec.conf:135`; `rom/exec/getmsg.c:40-55`). For a plain native `Message` placed on a port exposed to the guest, the thunk creates the 52-byte guest / 96-byte host IntuiMessage shadow and synchronizes IntuiMessage fields beyond the 48-byte native Message, including `IDCMPWindow` (`m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:2292-2308,2641-2652`; shadow creation at `rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_shadow.c:72-84`). The guest receives a pointer to the wrong record type, and shadow synchronization reads fields outside the generic Message object. This is conditional on `GetMsg()` returning a non-IntuiMessage from a native-backed port; IntuiMessage results are the intended supported case.

The handwritten `WaitPort()` bridge also returns the native `Message *` directly as the guest result (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks.c:609-619`), although the API returns the first queued message without removing it (`rom/exec/exec.conf:137`; `rom/exec/waitport.c:40-57`). Unlike `GetMsg()`, it does not create or look up a guest shadow. A guest that consumes the documented return value therefore receives a host pointer narrowed by the dispatcher instead of a guest address, and cannot reliably use it as a guest `Message *`. This applies whether the queued object is a generic Message or an IntuiMessage; callers that ignore WaitPort's return and then call GetMsg do not encounter this particular result-path defect.

The handwritten `ReplyMsg()` bridge only calls native Exec when A1 exactly matches a registered shadow (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks.c:643-652`). The public vector accepts any `struct Message *` (`rom/exec/exec.conf:136`), but an ordinary guest-owned Message has no shadow mapping and is silently ignored. Native `ReplyMsg()` sends a message with a non-NULL reply port back through `InternalPutMsg()` (`rom/exec/replymsg.c:50-64`); skipping the call leaves the sender without its reply and can leave it waiting. This is another conditional instance of the guest/native Message boundary; the current shadow path is limited to messages returned by the Intuition-oriented GetMsg thunk.

The generated Icon `GetIconRectangleA()` thunk also passes the guest-owned output `Rectangle *` directly through `THUNK_PTR()` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:4572-4581`). The native implementation writes `MinX`, `MinY`, `MaxX`, and `MaxY` as four 16-bit `WORD` values (`workbench/libs/icon/geticonrectangle.c:45-104`; `compiler/include/graphics/gfx.h:45-51`). On the supported little-endian hosts, an ordinary guest buffer remains big-endian, so each coordinate is returned byte-reversed when the guest reads it. The wrapper creates no Rectangle shadow; the local m68kemu layout table has no Rectangle entry. No maintained emulated guest caller was found.

The BOOPSI thunks expose the same unconverted object/class handles. `NewObjectA()` and `MakeClass()` return native pointers directly; `FindClass()` also returns its native class pointer, while `DisposeObject()`, `SetAttrsA()`, `GetAttr()`, `AddClass()`, `RemoveClass()`, and `FreeClass()` resolve their pointer arguments with `THUNK_PTR()` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:5725-5792`; public contracts in `rom/intuition/intuition.conf:162-176`). Native `NewObjectA()` returns the object dispatched by `OM_NEW`, which the public API says is later manipulated and released with these vectors (`rom/intuition/newobjecta.c:34-66`). On 64-bit hosts, a returned pointer is narrowed into guest D0 and is not registered as a shadow, so a guest cannot reliably use or dispose the object or class through the paired APIs. No maintained guest caller was found.

The `GetAttr()` thunk also forwards its guest `storagePtr` unchanged (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:5754-5761`), while the native API declares it `IPTR *` and passes it to the object's `OM_GET` method (`rom/intuition/intuition.conf:166`; `rom/intuition/getattr.c:20,70-78`). On supported 64-bit hosts, class methods that write an `IPTR` result use an eight-byte slot, but the m68k guest slot is four bytes; pointer-valued or other `IPTR` attributes can therefore overwrite the following guest word and store a value the guest cannot represent. The impact depends on the selected class attribute's documented storage type. No maintained emulated guest caller was found.

The `NextPubScreen()` thunk returns the native function's pointer result unchanged (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:5609-5615`), although the public API specifies that result as the caller-provided `namebuff` or NULL (`rom/intuition/intuition.conf:143`; `rom/intuition/nextpubscreen.c:23-35,88-95`). Its A1 buffer is resolved into the guest memory arena, so on 64-bit hosts native code returns the host address `ctx->mem + guest_address`; the dispatcher narrows that host pointer into guest D0 without `host_to_m68k()` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_moira.cpp:256-275`). A guest that uses the documented pointer result as a guest address therefore receives an unusable host-derived value. The only checked-in caller tests the result against NULL and then uses its separate local buffer, so this result-pointer consequence is not established for that caller. This conditional return-mapping defect is another EK9432 instance; no maintained emulated caller was found.

The generated `DrawImageState()` thunk resolves its A1 argument with `THUNK_PTR(1)` and passes it directly to native Intuition without creating an `Image` shadow (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:5693-5702`). The public structure is 20 bytes in the m68k guest layout and 40 bytes on the checked-in 64-bit host layout; `ImageData` is at offsets 10/16 and `NextImage` at 16/32 (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:2231-2236,4554`; declaration in `compiler/include/intuition/intuition.h:744-757`). Native `DrawImageState()` reads `Depth`, `PlanePick`, dimensions, and `ImageData`/`NextImage` from the host offsets (`rom/intuition/drawimagestate.c:98,137-157,217-240,292`), so a guest-owned ordinary `Image` is interpreted using the wrong field positions and pointer widths. This can select incorrect draw parameters or follow an unrelated guest field as `NextImage`, rather than reliably drawing the supplied image. The issue is conditional on an emulated caller passing a guest-owned `Image`; returned/native-backed images with an existing appropriate shadow are a different path. No maintained emulated caller was found. This is another structure-marshalling instance of EK9432.

The generated Intuition `SetPointer()` thunk also passes the guest's legacy cursor bitmap bytes without conversion: it resolves A1 with `THUNK_PTR(1)` and calls native `SetPointer()` directly (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:5265-5275`; public signature in `rom/intuition/intuition.conf:97`). Native `SetPointer()` routes the data through `MakePointerFromData()` and `PointerClass`, which requests `SPRITEA_OldDataFormat` from `AllocSpriteDataA()` (`rom/intuition/setpointer.c:58-60`; `rom/intuition/misc.c:250-264`; `rom/intuition/pointerclass.c:51-66,84-104`). In that format, `AllocSpriteDataA()` reads each source row as two native `UWORD`s, applies `AROS_WORD2BE()`, and stores those words into planar bitmap memory (`rom/graphics/allocspritedataa.c:164-193`). On little-endian hosts this transforms guest bytes such as `80 01` into planar bytes `01 80`; `BitMapScale()` subsequently reads the plane byte-by-byte with the first bit in each byte representing the leftmost pixel (`rom/graphics/bitmapscale.c:340-357`). Thus an ordinary guest cursor row with an asymmetric 16-bit pattern is horizontally rearranged within its two bytes. This applies to emulated guest calls with legacy sprite-format cursor data on little-endian m68kemu hosts; no maintained guest caller was found. It is another input-data byte-order case of EK9432, not an independent root cause.

The generated DataTypes `DoDTDomainA()` thunk passes its A4 `domain` pointer through `THUNK_PTR()` directly to native code (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:899-910`; configured vector `workbench/libs/datatypes/datatypes.conf:64`, registered at LVO 306 in `m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:7233-7266`). The native implementation copies the successful `GM_DOMAIN` result to `*domain` (`workbench/libs/datatypes/dodtdomaina.c:78-92`). `IBox` is four 16-bit fields (`Left`, `Top`, `Width`, `Height`) and is eight bytes on both guest and host (`compiler/include/intuition/intuition.h:840-846`; `rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:1844-1849`), so this does not establish an overwrite. But `THUNK_PTR()` only resolves a shadow or maps ordinary guest memory (`m68kemu_thunks.h:37`; `m68kemu_intern.h:115-125`), and the thunk performs no word conversion. On the supported little-endian hosts, a successful native domain write leaves each coordinate's two bytes reversed for the big-endian m68k guest. The selected `workbench-datatypes-sound` module implements `GM_DOMAIN`; `Sound_DOMAIN()` writes the resulting `IBox` and returns `TRUE` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/mmakefile.src:7-14`; `sound/sound.conf:27-28`; `sound/dispatch.c:323-324,1467-1494`). A source search found no checked-in caller of the public `DoDTDomainA()` vector, so the guest invocation remains conditional. This is another conditional output-byte-order instance of EK9432. This call has a second, independent marshalling omission: its A5 `attrs` parameter is a `struct TagItem *` by the configured vector signature, but the generated wrapper resolves it with `THUNK_PTR(5)` and forwards it unchanged (`m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:899-910`; `workbench/libs/datatypes/datatypes.conf:64`). The native implementation stores that pointer in `gpDomain.gpd_Attrs` and dispatches `GM_DOMAIN` (`workbench/libs/datatypes/dodtdomaina.c:78-88`); a method that reads the attributes then interprets guest-width, big-endian TagItems as native records. On 64-bit hosts the guest entries are 8 bytes while native entries are 16 bytes; on little-endian hosts even matching-width records have reversed tag/data fields. The thunk should use `m68k_to_native_taglist()` and free the temporary after the synchronous dispatch. No checked-in caller of this public vector was found, so this remains conditional on an emulated caller with a usable object whose domain method consumes attributes; no in-tree effect is claimed.

DOS `GetArgStr()` and `SetArgStr()` also exchange raw argument-string pointers with emulated callers. The generated `GetArgStr()` thunk returns the native `Process.pr_Arguments` value directly as `IPTR` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:1349-1353`; implementation `rom/dos/getargstr.c:47-54`). `SetArgStr()` maps D1 to a host pointer into the guest arena, installs that host pointer as `pr_Arguments`, and returns the previous native pointer unchanged (`m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:1355-1359`; implementation `rom/dos/setargstr.c:50-56`). The public contract requires callers to restore the original argument string before process exit (`setargstr.c:25-33`). Since D0 is narrowed to 32 bits and returned pointers are not translated back to guest addresses, the guest cannot reliably read `GetArgStr()` or `SetArgStr()` results or restore the old string through the next thunk. **Trigger and consequence:** guest software retrieves or swaps its current process argument string through either DOS vector; the returned pointer may be truncated or treated as an unrelated guest-arena offset, so string access or restoration fails. **Affected configuration:** optional m68kemu on supported 64-bit hosts when a guest calls these DOS vectors. No checked-in emulated caller was found. This is another EK9432 pointer-round-trip case.

DataTypes `FindToolNodeA()` also crosses both sides of this boundary: the generated wrapper maps `toollist` and `attrs` only with `THUNK_PTR()` and returns the native `ToolNode *` as `IPTR` (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:810-815`). On supported 64-bit hosts, a guest `TagItem` is an 8-byte, big-endian pair while native `TagItem` uses the host `IPTR` alignment/width (`compiler/include/utility/tagitem.h:17-23`; `m68kemu_intern.h:115-125`); `FindToolNodeA()` reads those tags with `GetTagData()` and traverses `toollist` with `ForeachNode()` before returning a node (`workbench/libs/datatypes/findtoolnodea.c:73-105`). Guest-provided lists and filter arrays therefore are not valid native structures, and any result pointer is not translated back into a guest address. **Trigger and consequence:** an emulated m68k caller supplies an ordinary non-NULL guest tool list and/or filter tags to `FindToolNodeA()`; the native routine may fail to match or follow invalid host-layout links, and a returned node pointer is unusable as a guest handle. **Affected configuration:** optional m68kemu library on supported 64-bit hosts, when guest software calls this DataTypes vector. No checked-in native caller proves an emulated use case. This is another EK9432 marshalling instance, not a separate root cause.

DataTypes `GetDTString()` also returns an unconverted native pointer from its generated thunk (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:795-800`; public result contract and LVO in `workbench/libs/datatypes/datatypes.conf:51`; implementation `workbench/libs/datatypes/getdtstring.c:50-108`). The implementation returns a catalog string or one of its native static fallback strings. The thunk returns that host `STRPTR` as `IPTR`; the emulator dispatcher narrows it into guest D0 without reverse mapping (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_moira.cpp:256-275`). A guest that dereferences the documented result therefore treats a host address (possibly truncated) as a guest-memory offset, rather than receiving a guest string pointer. A repository C-source search found checked-in native callers in Identify, MultiView, and a developer demo, but no emulated guest caller. This is a further conditional pointer-return instance of EK9432.

DataTypes method-table helpers have a related input, return, and release mismatch. `CopyDTMethods()` and `CopyDTTriggerMethods()` pass their guest arrays directly through `THUNK_PTR()` and return the native `AllocVec()` result unchanged (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:844-860`; implementations `workbench/libs/datatypes/copydtmethods.c:61-121` and `copydttriggermethods.c:67-131`). On little-endian hosts, the former reads guest big-endian `ULONG` IDs as host values; the latter reads guest `DTMethod` records at host offsets/stride despite the recorded 12-byte guest versus 24-byte native layouts (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:760-767,4468`). The returned native allocation is not converted back to a guest pointer. The paired `FreeDTMethods()` thunk resolves that returned D0 value with `THUNK_PTR()` before calling `FreeVec()` (`m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:862-867`); if the truncated value is outside the guest arena the resolver returns NULL and `FreeVec()` safely does nothing, leaking the allocation, while an in-range value is interpreted as an unrelated guest offset. These helper pairs therefore cannot safely copy, use, and release ordinary guest-owned method tables on the supported 64-bit m68kemu targets. The checked-in `sound` class's Copy/Free calls use native arrays and do not exercise the emulated path; no guest caller was found. This is another conditional method-table instance of EK9432.

The DataTypes method-table getters also return raw native pointers. `GetDTMethods()` and `GetDTTriggerMethods()` obtain `DTA_Methods`/`DTA_TriggerMethods` into native pointer locals and return them (`workbench/libs/datatypes/getdtmethods.c:57-71`; `getdttriggermethods.c:65-78`); their generated thunks return those values unchanged (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:739-750`). The dispatcher narrows each result to guest D0 without reverse mapping (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_moira.cpp:256-275`). Passing a returned table to `FindMethod()`/`FindTriggerMethod()` cannot round-trip: those wrappers resolve A0 as a guest address (`m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:827-841`), and the native finders then dereference the resulting pointer (`workbench/libs/datatypes/findmethod.c:57-68`; `findtriggermethod.c:63-89`). Checked-in native MultiView, Play and Print callers use native objects and are unaffected; no emulated guest caller was found. This is another conditional native-pointer return and handle round-trip instance of EK9432.

DataTypes `ObtainDTDrawInfoA()` has an unconverted tag-list input: its generated thunk resolves A1 with `THUNK_PTR()` and forwards it unchanged (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:763-770`). The selected Sound datatype's `Sound_OBTAINDRAWINFO()` reads `PDTA_Screen` and `GA_DrawInfo` from `ops_AttrList` using native `GetTagData()` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c:249,353-354,4161-4168`; registered by `sound/sound.conf:27-28`). On the supported 64-bit host, a guest `TagItem` is 8 bytes and native `TagItem` is 16 (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:3740-3746,4651`); native tag iteration therefore reads the guest fields at the wrong endian, width, and stride and can skip the guest terminator. The Sound method can then miss both requested drawing pointers and return FALSE, leaving its draw state unobtained. The checked-in BoingIconBar caller supplies `attrs == NULL` and only tests the result (`workbench/tools/BoingIconBar/iconbar.c:948-955`), so it does not trigger this case; no emulated guest caller was found. The guest trigger also requires a usable DataTypes object pointer. This is another conditional raw guest-tag-list instance of EK9432.

DataTypes `PrintDTObjectA()` forwards the guest `dtPrint *` unchanged from its generated thunk (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:753-760`; vector signature in `workbench/libs/datatypes/datatypes.conf:47`). The guest structure is 16 bytes, while the native 64-bit-host structure is 32 bytes; its three pointer fields move from guest offsets 4/8/12 to native offsets 8/16/24 (`compiler/include/datatypes/datatypesclass.h:412-418`; `rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:4168-4173`). `THUNK_PTR()` resolves the address to an existing shadow or the guest arena but does not construct a `dtPrint` shadow (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks.h:37`; `m68kemu_intern.h:114-125`). Native `PrintDTObjectA()` copies `*msg` by value into its asynchronous message (`workbench/libs/datatypes/printdtobjecta.c:123-132,183-204`), and `AsyncPrinter()` later dereferences `dtp_PIO` in `CopyMem()` (`:62-68`). The native copy therefore reads pointer fields at incompatible offsets, including `dtp_PIO` from beyond the guest's 16-byte record; the async worker can read an invalid/unrelated address instead of the guest printer I/O request. This applies to a guest call with a usable DataTypes object and ordinary guest-owned `dtPrint` on the optional 64-bit-host m68kemu configuration. The repository search found no checked-in caller of `PrintDTObjectA()`; native callers do not exercise this thunk. This is another conditional structure-marshalling instance of EK9432.

DataTypes `DoAsyncLayout()` also forwards its guest `gpLayout *` directly (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:713-718`; vector declaration in `workbench/libs/datatypes/datatypes.conf:42`). The m68k record is 12 bytes, while its native 64-bit-host form is 24 bytes; `gpl_GInfo` moves from offset 4 to 8 and `gpl_Initial` from offset 8 to 16 (`compiler/include/intuition/gadgetclass.h:337-345`; `rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_shadow_layouts.h:4237-4242`). The thunk resolves the guest address but creates no `gpLayout` shadow. Native `DoAsyncLayout()` immediately passes `gpl->gpl_GInfo` to `Do_OM_NOTIFY()` and dereferences `gpl->gpl_GInfo->gi_Window`, then copies the record and `GadgetInfo` for the worker (`workbench/libs/datatypes/doasynclayout.c:174-189`). These reads use host offsets against the guest record, so a guest-supplied layout message can produce an invalid `GadgetInfo` pointer before asynchronous layout starts. This applies to a guest call with a valid DataTypes object and ordinary guest-owned `gpLayout`; the in-tree MultiView call is disabled by `#if 0`, and the selected Picture caller passes a native message, so no checked-in emulated caller was established. This is another conditional structure-marshalling instance of EK9432.

DataTypes `GetDTAttrsA()` converts the guest TagItem array but not the width or representation of its output values (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:681-688`; converter at `rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_shadow.c:139-163`). The converter maps an in-range guest `ti_Data` storage address to `ctx->mem + address`, then native `GetDTAttrsA()` casts it to `IPTR *` and dispatches `OM_GET` (`workbench/libs/datatypes/getdtattrsa.c:83-91`). On a 64-bit host, a guest output slot is 32-bit, but the base DataTypes `OM_GET` writes native-width `IPTR` values through that pointer; for `DTA_Domain`, it stores the native `dto_Domain` pointer (`workbench/libs/datatypes/class.c:318-355,560-562`). A successful query can therefore overwrite the following guest word and leave a truncated host pointer in the output slot. This applies when a guest call supplies a valid DataTypes object and an output slot in guest memory; the object handle itself must be usable, a boundary already affected by EK9432's unconverted object-return paths. No maintained emulated guest caller was found. This is another conditional output-width and pointer-marshalling instance of EK9432.

The generated diskfont thunks add two more concrete instances. `AvailFonts()` passes its guest output buffer directly to native code (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:914-920`), while `BufferInfoCreate()` and `BufferInfoAdd()` lay out native `struct AvailFonts`/`TAvailFonts` records and native `TagItem` arrays in that buffer (`workbench/libs/diskfont/availfonts.c:149-215`; declarations in `compiler/include/diskfont/diskfont.h:78-96` and `compiler/include/graphics/text.h:72-88`). On a 64-bit host, `TextAttr`/`TTextAttr` pointer fields and record sizes differ from the 32-bit m68k guest layout; on little-endian hosts, the UWORD fields and tag values also retain host byte order. A guest cannot reliably parse those returned records. Separately, `NewFontContents()` returns a host allocation directly through guest D0 and `DisposeFontContents()` later resolves its A1 input with `THUNK_PTR()` (`m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:923-936`); the `FontContentsHeader` and entries have pointer-free fixed-width fields, but the native allocation still has no guest handle/shadow round trip, so a guest cannot reliably dispose or dereference that result. These findings are conditional on guest use of the optional diskfont vectors; no maintained emulated caller was identified. The public vector declarations and native implementations are selected in `workbench/libs/diskfont/diskfont.conf:13-19` and `workbench/libs/diskfont/mmakefile.src:5-13`.

**Trigger and consequence:** an m68k guest calls one of the returned-object APIs through the generated Icon or IFFParse thunks and then uses, returns, or dereferences the object; calls diskfont `AvailFonts()` and consumes the returned records, or calls `NewFontContents()` and then reads or disposes its returned header; calls Utility `SetMem()` and consumes its documented destination-pointer result; calls DataTypes `GetDTString()` and dereferences its returned string pointer; calls DataTypes `PrintDTObjectA()` with an ordinary guest `dtPrint` and usable DataTypes object; calls DataTypes `DoAsyncLayout()` with an ordinary guest `gpLayout` and usable `GadgetInfo`; calls DataTypes `GetDTAttrsA()` with a guest output slot for a pointer-valued attribute such as `DTA_Domain`; calls DataTypes `ObtainDTDrawInfoA()` with guest TagItems; calls DataTypes `GetDTMethods()`/`GetDTTriggerMethods()` and passes a returned table to `FindMethod()`/`FindTriggerMethod()`; calls DataTypes `CopyDTMethods()`/`CopyDTTriggerMethods()` on guest method tables and uses/releases the result; passes an ordinary guest-owned `DateStamp` to Locale `FormatDate()`/`ParseDate()` or DOS `SetFileDate()`, or calls DOS `DateStamp()` and consumes its output fields or returned pointer; calls DOS `Info()` with a guest-owned `InfoData` buffer; calls Utility `Amiga2Date()`/`Date2Amiga()`/`CheckDate()` with a guest `ClockData`; calls DataTypes `DoDTDomainA()` with a guest `IBox` on a little-endian host and receives a successful domain result; calls Commodities `CopyBrokerList()`/`FreeBrokerList()` with a guest-owned `List`; uses `GetSegListInfo()` with a matching tracked segment and a guest output slot for `GSLI_ElfHandle`/`GSLI_68KHUNK`; locks and iterates the DOS list through `LockDosList()`/`AttemptLockDosList()` and `FindDosEntry()`/`NextDosEntry()`; calls Exec list primitives on guest-owned `List`/`Node` structures; calls Exec `PutMsg()` with an ordinary guest-owned `Message`; receives a plain generic `Message` through the handwritten `GetMsg()` thunk; calls `ReplyMsg()` with an ordinary guest-owned `Message` that has no shadow; consumes the `WaitPort()` return value as a guest pointer; calls `Allocate()`/`Deallocate()` or `AllocEntry()`/`FreeEntry()` with guest memory-list structures; reads the returned record from `FindVar()`; consumes `FilePart()`/`PathPart()`/`NextPubScreen()` results as guest pointers; or calls DOS `ErrorReport()` with `REPORT_VOLUME` or `REPORT_INSERT` and a guest-owned volume record/name while requesters are enabled; calls Icon `GetIconRectangleA()` or Intuition `QueryOverscan()`/`GadgetMouse()` with guest-owned coordinate output storage; calls Intuition `SetPointerBounds()` with guest Rectangle input, `SetPointer()` with guest legacy cursor bitmap data, `DrawImageState()` with a guest-owned `Image`, or keymap `MapRawKey()` with a guest `InputEvent`; calls `GetPrefs()`/`GetDefPrefs()`/`SetPrefs()` using guest preference records; uses `GetScreenData()` and consumes its copied `Screen` structure; calls BOOPSI `NewObjectA()`/`MakeClass()`/`FindClass()` and then uses or disposes the returned handle; or calls `GetAttr()` for an `IPTR`-sized attribute into a guest storage slot. These outputs/inputs retain big-endian guest values, native-layout Screen fields, unrepresentable native handles, or host-width attribute writes. It also includes guest calls to Intuition `SetIPrefs()`, and `SysReqHandler()` calls that receive a matching IDCMP event; the latter APIs have no maintained emulated caller in this checkout. For these ErrorReport cases, native code reads the wrong DeviceList offsets or treats a guest address as a host string pointer. The pointer-return paths produce an unusable pointer or an object with the wrong layout, disrupting guest-side object access and ownership. `NextPubScreen()` is affected only when the guest consumes its returned buffer pointer rather than using the buffer argument directly. On little-endian hosts, `FormatDate()` can interpret byte-reversed date fields and `ParseDate()` can leave byte-reversed results in guest memory, and DOS `DateStamp()` can return byte-reversed fields in guest memory. The exact pointer symptom depends on the truncated address and guest-memory layout; no claim is made that every pointer call faults. `NextObject()` also interprets and writes its guest pointer slot with native width and byte order, so iteration state and the adjacent guest word can be corrupted on selected little-endian 64-bit hosts. `SetPointer()` can rearrange asymmetric cursor rows within each two-byte word on little-endian hosts. `DrawImageState()` interprets guest-owned `Image` records at native offsets and pointer widths. `GetMsg()` additionally interprets a generic Message using the larger IntuiMessage layout, `ReplyMsg()` drops unshadowed guest messages, and `WaitPort()` returns the native address without reverse mapping; a caller that ignores the WaitPort result and obtains the same message via GetMsg is only affected by the GetMsg type assumption if the message is generic.
